messages:
acme_sre: Hey team — since the IdP cert rotation at ~23:18 UTC we've had ~10% of SSO logins fail with 403. Affected tenant: acme-prod. Error in our proxy logs: "AssertionConsumerService URL mismatch / signature thumbprint not found". Can you triage?

devon: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the exact error snippet / SAML response (redact PII) and confirm if this started immediately after the IdP rotated certs? Also which IdP endpoint are you pointing at?

acme_sre: Yep started right after rotation. Here's the relevant assertion fragment we captured (thumbprints redacted):

<ds:Signature>...</ds:Signature>
<!-- verify error -->
Signature verification failed: certificate thumbprint 0xDEADBEEF not found in current metadata

alex: Two quick guesses: 1) our metadata poller didn't pick up the new KeyDescriptor; 2) the IdP served metadata via a 302 + compressed response and the watcher dropped the new key because of an encoding/redirect edge-case. Can you run a raw fetch from your edge?

acme_sre: Run this on our side and pasted output:

$ curl -i -L 'https://idp.acme.com/metadata' -H 'Accept-Encoding: br,gzip' -o meta.xml
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: http://idp-backup.acme.internal/metadata
...
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Encoding: br
Content-Type: application/samlmetadata+xml
ETag: "v3-2026-03-16"

When we saved meta.xml and inspected it the new <KeyDescriptor> with the rotated cert is present.

devon: Thanks. Can you also share our redwood metadata-watcher logs for the tenant around 23:15-23:25? We need to see whether the watcher followed the 302 and decompressed correctly. If it's a watcher bug we can force a refresh.

sre-bot: metadata-watcher[acme-prod]: fetch start ts=2026-03-16T23:14:45Z accept-encoding=br,gzip
metadata-watcher: fetch -> 302 to http://idp-backup.acme.internal/metadata (followed)
metadata-watcher: response content-encoding=br status=200 etag: "v3-2026-03-15" -> parse ok
metadata-watcher: parsed keys count=1 ; new keys detected=0

maria: That log looks suspicious: ETag shows yesterday's value even though curl returned a new ETag. Possible race where CDN returned stale ETag to the poller due to redirect/probe. Two paths: force metadata refresh for tenant now, and add a short-term workaround to accept both old/new thumbprints during propagation window. I'll own the fix if this is watcher behavior.

devon: Workarounds: 1) tenant admin can run a forced refresh: 
$ redwood-sso admin fetch-metadata --tenant acme-prod --force
2) temporary allow both thumbprints for 10 minutes via admin CLI: 
$ redwood-sso admin set-allowed-thumbprints --tenant acme-prod --thumbprints "OLDTHUMB,NEWTHUMB" --grace 600

acme_sre: Running the forced fetch now...

sre-bot: admin-action: fetch-metadata --tenant acme-prod --force -> success (fetched new metadata, reloaded cache)

acme_sre: After forced refresh, our error rate dropped from ~10% to ~0.5%. Some clients still hit 403s but much better.

maria: Good. I'll open ENG ticket ENG-987 to patch metadata-watcher: follow 302s consistently, respect content-encoding on final response even when redirects occur, and verify ETag derivation. Proposed short-term patch: when ETag differs between redirect hops, prefer the final response ETag and bypass stale-cache short-circuit for one poll cycle. Also adding a one-time backfill run for tenants that reported failures.

alex: For triage we should also look for any intermediary caching (CDN/proxy) that strips or rewrites Accept-Encoding on the poller requests. If the poller loses br/gzip then the backend might respond differently. I'll add extra debug logs and a retry path.

janelle: I've scheduled a maintenance window to run a one-off metadata backfill for all tenants that had a metadata ETag change in the last 24h. I'll also coordinate with infra to allow a temporary two-thumbprint grace window for affected tenants (admin page + CLI).

acme_sre: Confirming after the temporary allowlist and forced fetch our customer logins are back to normal for 2h. Thanks for the fast help! :tada:

devon: Great — follow-ups: ENG-987 (watcher patch), OPS-221 (backfill job), and update KB article "SSO: metadata watcher redirect/encoding issues" with the workaround commands. Assigning to maria and janelle.

maria: I'll push a hotfix branch with tests for redirect+encoding cases and a canary rollout to metadata-watcher. If anyone sees residual 403s after next hour, re-open here and paste one sample assertion.

acme_sre: Will do. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

sre-bot: ticket created: ENG-987, OPS-221, KB-455

devon: Closing the thread for now — reopening if any new failures. Thanks everyone.
